title: Enterprise Onboarding: Support Process, Health Checks, QBR & Known Issues Playbook
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the enterprise onboarding runbook, support process, escalation paths, integration checklist, known issues and workarounds, and the health-check / QBR (Quarterly Business Review) cadence for Redwood Inference customers. It is intended for Customer Success, Support Engineers, Solutions Engineering, and SRE partners who run onboarding and ongoing operational health for enterprise accounts.

Scope

- Applies to all enterprise customers onboarding to Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Covers the first 90 days (detailed milestones) and ongoing periodic health checks and QBRs.
- Does not replace product-specific runbooks (see related pages).

Goals

- Reduce time-to-first-successful-production-call to under 14 days.
- Establish clear SLAs and escalation contact points for Sev{0-3} incidents.
- Maintain operational health metrics and a repeatable QBR agenda for strategic customers.

Quick Links

- Integration checklist (section below)
- Escalation matrix and response SLAs
- Known issues & workarounds
- QBR agenda and templates

1) Onboarding timeline (30/60/90)

30-day (Initial Validation)
1. Kickoff meeting: introduce CSM, Solutions Engineer (SE), and primary technical contact. Confirm success criteria.
2. Access & Entitlements: ensure API keys, org roles, and console access. Validate network allowlists for Hosted or Dedicated IPs.
3. Basic integration: send sample requests, validate responses, confirm rate limits and auth flows.
4. First health check: baseline latency, p50/p95, error rate, and cost estimate.

60-day (Integration & Load Validation)
1. Integration completion: webhooks, callbacks, and observability hooks (tracing/logging) integrated.
2. Load testing: staged traffic ramp with SRE/Platform support; validate autoscaling and Dedicated pool behavior.
3. Quality validation: run smoke evals on canonical prompt sets; register baseline metrics.
4. Security review: required artifacts for Private deployments or regulated customers (KMS integration, audit log verification).

90-day (Production Readiness & Handoff)
1. Final cutover plan and rollback strategy agreed.
2. Operational runbook shared: monitoring dashboards, alert thresholds, and runbook links.
3. QBR scheduling and KPIs confirmed.
4. Handoff to ongoing support with agreed SLOs and escalation path.

2) Integration checklist (pre-integration & production)

Pre-integration items
- Product contacts: CSM, SE, Technical Lead, Security/Compliance rep.
- Accounts & access: API key issued to integration environment; role-based access validated.
- Network: IP allowlist (hosted) or VPC peering config (Dedicated/Private).
- Secrets: KMS/HSM integration plan for Private deployments.

Integration items
- Model selection & pinning: agree model family + version for production route.
- Rate limits & quotas: confirm per-route limits, burst policies, and billing expectations.
- Observability: add tracing headers, export logs to customer SIEM (if requested), and configure per-route dashboards.
- Metrics & telemetry: instrument request/response latency, token usage, error codes, and model output quality signals.
- Test prompts & evals: define 50 canonical prompts for regression monitoring.

Sample minimal API sanity check (example)
- POST /v1/generate with auth header: verify 200, tokens billed, response shape.

3) Escalation playbook (severity definitions & paths)

Severity matrix
- Sev 0 / P0: Platform-wide outage affecting all customers (e.g., control plane down, large Dedicated pool failure).
  - Response SLA: 15 minutes to acknowledge, 60 minutes for remediation plan.
  - Contacts: SRE on-call, Platform Eng Lead, Head of Support.
- Sev 1 / P1: Customer-impacting outage for a production tenant (e.g., model endpoint returning 5xx for >5% of requests).
  - Response SLA: 30 minutes to acknowledge, 4 hours for mitigation plan.
  - Contacts: CS lead, Customer's technical emergency contact, SRE/Serving runtime on-call.
- Sev 2 / P2: Degraded behavior with workarounds (e.g., latency spikes, increased 429s).
  - Response SLA: 4 business hours to acknowledge, 48 hours for remediation plan.
- Sev 3 / P3: Non-urgent bugs, feature requests, onboarding questions.
  - Response SLA: 1 business day to acknowledge, resolution per backlog prioritization.

Escalation steps (numbered procedure)
1. Triage: Support engineer collects artifacts (request id, timestamps, sample inputs/outputs, console logs, route config, model version).
2. Reproduce: Attempt to reproduce in staging with identical inputs.
3. Mitigate: Apply short-term mitigation (route fallback, reduced concurrency, request throttling, or reroute to compatible model variant).
4. Notify: Update customer via agreed channel (Slack, PagerDuty incident, or email) every 60 minutes for Sev 0/1 until resolved.
5. Root cause & retrospective: Postmortem authored for Sev 0/1 within 7 days; shared with customer and internal stakeholders.

4) Support process (ticket lifecycle and artifact requirements)

Ticket lifecycle
- New ticket: Capture summary, severity, environment (prod/staging), route/model id, timestamps, and customer impact.
- Triage: Assign owner within 1 business hour for P1/P2, within 1 business day for P3.
- Investigation: Attach request ids, request/response pairs, console logs, and any recent deploy/change IDs.
- Resolution: Document fix, mitigation steps, and preventions. Close ticket after customer confirmation or 7 days with no reply.

Required ticket attachments
- Request ID(s) and timestamp range
- Route configuration snapshot (route_id, model, tokenization settings, batching config)
- Error logs and stack traces (anonymize sensitive data)
- If applicable: packet captures, network logs, or VPC flow logs for networking issues

Support SLAs (customer-facing) - sample table
| Severity | Acknowledge SLA | Update cadence | Target resolution |
|----------|-----------------|----------------|-------------------|
| P0 | 15 minutes | 15 min | 4 hours (mitigation), 72 hours (root cause) |
| P1 | 30 minutes | 60 min | 24-72 hours |
| P2 | 4 hours | 4-8 hours | 3-7 days |
| P3 | 1 business day | 2 business days | Next release / backlog |

5) Known issues & workarounds (living list)

- Issue: Intermittent p95 latency spikes for short-sequence requests on Dedicated pools.
  Workaround: Temporarily increase minimum workers for the pool, enable request-deprioritization, or route to a lower-quantized model. Action owner: Serving Runtime SRE.
- Issue: Embeddings batch endpoint returns 429 when sending mixed batch sizes.
  Workaround: Normalize batch sizes client-side (pad or split requests to uniform sizes) and enable client-side retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries). Action owner: SDK/DevEx.
- Issue: Discrepancy in billed tokens vs. observed tokens in SDK during streaming responses.
  Workaround: Collect request ids and attach streaming chunk logs; switch to non-streaming endpoint for billing reconciliation. Action owner: Billing + Support.
- Issue: Model regression after auto-update to new model variant.
  Workaround: Roll back to pinned model version; require canary testing for future model rollouts. Action owner: Product + Model Onboarding.

Known-issues process
1. Add issue to Known Issues dashboard with severity and affected customers.
2. Author workaround and publish to customer-facing KB if broadly applicable.
3. Track fix in engineering backlog and link to ticket.

6) Health checks & QBR materials (metrics, cadence, agenda)

Operational health metrics (track weekly/monthly)
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 per route.
- Error rate: 4xx and 5xx by route and by model.
- Token usage: tokens per 1k requests, cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Throughput: requests/sec and peak concurrency.
- Quality: prompt-set eval pass rate, hallucination rate (where measurable).
- Availability: uptime percentage (monthly).

SLOs (example)
| Metric | Target | Alert threshold | Owner |
|--------|--------|-----------------|-------|
| Uptime | 99.9% | <99.8% (7 day) | Platform SRE |
| p95 latency | <450ms (hosted) | >700ms (1 hour) | Serving Runtime |
| Error rate | <0.5% | >1% (30 min) | Support |

QBR cadence & pre-work
- Cadence: Quarterly for strategic customers; monthly health calls for top-tier customers.
- Pre-QBR checklist (to be completed 7 days prior):
  - Export last 90 days of operational metrics.
  - Run regression tests on canonical prompt set and attach results.
  - Compile change-log of major deploys, config changes, and incidents.
  - Collect open action items and their owners.

QBR agenda (90 minutes)
1. Introductions & agenda (5 min)
2. Business outcomes & success metrics review (10 min)
3. Operational health (latency, errors, availability) (20 min)
4. Cost & usage trends (billing insights) (15 min)
5. Model quality & evals (15 min)
6. Roadmap & upcoming changes (10 min)
7. Risks, open issues, and action items (10 min)
8. Next steps & meeting cadence (5 min)

Deliverables after QBR
- QBR slide deck (shared within 3 business days)
- Action item tracker with owners and deadlines
- Updated runbook if any operational changes were agreed

7) Handoffs, ownership, and RACI

RACI summary (text table)
- Customer Success (CSM) — Responsible for success criteria, QBR scheduling, and customer communications.
- Support — Responsible for triage, mitigation, and ticket resolution.
- SRE / Serving Runtime — Accountable for platform health, incident response, and root cause.
- Product / Model Onboarding — Consulted on model upgrades and regressions.
- Security / Compliance — Informed for Private deployments and audits.

8) Templates & example communications

Incident notification (template)
Subject: [INCIDENT] {customer} {Sev} {summary}
Body: Short summary, impact, estimated scope, mitigation steps taken, next update time. Attach: request ids, logs, and runbook link.

QBR invite (template)
Subject: QBR — {Customer Name} — {Quarter} — {date}
Body: Agenda, required pre-reads (metrics export, regression results), and attendees.
